BA.rationale: Boeing shows a genuine but fragile earnings inflection — Q1 2026 revenue +14% YoY to $22.22B and near-breakeven net income (-$0.11 EPS) are directionally positive. However, the recovery is severely impaired on multiple fronts: (1) Operating income actually declined YoY from $461M in Q1 2025 to $448M in Q1 2026, contradicting the 'inflection' narrative on a YoY basis; (2) Operating cash flow remains deeply negative at -$179M (GAAP) or -$1.5B (non-GAAP FCF per Boeing), meaning the P&L recovery has not translated to cash generation; (3) The balance sheet carries 7.8x debt-to-equity with only $5.99B equity against $46.96B debt — any material charge erodes the equity cushion; (4) At 80.5x diluted PE with a 1.2% earnings yield versus 4.41% 10-year Treasuries, the stock embeds massive forward expectations with zero margin of safety; (5) BCA operating margin is still -6.1%, and Airbus holds structural advantages in narrowbody market share (~60% vs ~40%) and production rates (targeting 820 deliveries vs Boeing's 560-600); (6) Oil at $98-114/bbl pressures airline economics and could slow order momentum; (7) The stock sits at the 72nd percentile of its 251-day range ($176.77-$254.35), meaning the recovery is already partially priced. The risk-reward is deeply unfavorable: upside from continued execution is offset by extreme downside sensitivity to any earnings miss, production disruption, or demand shock, and the valuation offers no cushion. This is a recovery bet at a premium price, not a value proposition.

Airbus A320neo ~60% narrowbody market share vs 737 MAX ~40%; Airbus targets 820 deliveries in 2026 vs Boeing's 560-600
